To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the participation rate in a health examination study of older people is low (about 50 %), that non-participation is related to a wide range of factors, and that the main reason is that the participants are too old or too ill.
non-participation in health examinations is substantial and selection bias is present.
non-participation in the baseline survey was high (40.6%) and was associated with older age, lower education, lower health-related quality-of-life, and foreign citizenship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of non-response in health examination surveys of the population 75+ years.
the question: how do we get a representative sample of the older population?
the question whether the health examination survey is representative of the population 75+ years in Amsterdam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-responders in this study were more likely to have lower health-related quality-of-life than the participants.
the non-participants were more likely to be older, more frail and more disabled.
a substantial proportion of the elderly are missed in a health examination, and the reasons for this are complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-participation in health examinations in the elderly population is not random and that it is important for public health monitoring to take into account the reasons for non-participants.
the non-participation rate of a health examination survey in the population 85+ years is high, and the reasons are diverse.
the non-participant group is heterogeneous in its health problems, and that there are several barriers to participation, including the lack of interest in participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-participation is a major problem that can only be overcome by innovative study designs.
it is essential to include a wide range of health-related outcomes in the analysis of selection bias.
the reasons for non-participating in a health examination are very heterogeneous.
